excluded.label: decorates
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — the csharp-annotation precedent: an annotation is PASSIVE METADATA a tool reads, and a decorator is an APPLIED CALLABLE; a `decorates` row for a MATLAB attribute list would assert an application the vocabulary does not credit). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND ITS RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the vendored grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json) carries 148 node types of which 76 are named, and 0 of the 76 is a decorator/annotation production that wraps or applies to a declaration; the grammar DOES carry `attribute` and `attributes` (2 of the 76 named types), and those are exactly the class the adjudicated ontology holds to be passive metadata — a parenthesised ACCESS-SPECIFICATION list (`properties (SetAccess=private)`, `methods (Static)`) that the runtime reads off the declaration, never a callable applied to it. R3 (express on an existing node type) therefore EXISTS on `attributes` and is NOT TAKEN for the ONTOLOGICAL reason, never for difficulty: publishing `decorates property -> SetAccess` would credit metadata with an application. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (admitted files [0,3) of 3, transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): attributes lists 0, attribute entries 0, distinct attribute spellings 0 — the opportunity is counted, and it is 0 in this population because no admitted file is genuine MATLAB. THE DOABILITY HALF IS PINNED ELSEWHERE, NOT LOST: the fixture validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/class-surface.m exercises `properties (SetAccess=private)` and `methods (Access=private)` and the analyzer publishes the resulting VISIBILITY on the property/method symbols rather than inventing a relationship. FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): (1) a decorator/annotation production in the SERVED grammar that APPLIES to a declaration — counted 0 of the 76 named node types; the census line turning non-zero refutes the ruling; (2) an attribute site in the admitted population whose attribute is invoked as a callable applied to the declaration — counted 0 of 0 attribute sites in 0 of 3 files.

excluded.label: renders
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — MATLAB has no markup/component template construct, and the only component-shaped model it has is App Designer, whose UI is a CONTAINER TREE OF WIDGET CONSTRUCTOR CALLS inside a `.mlapp` archive, not a component symbol a file-scoped analyzer can render). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND THE RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the served grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json, 148 node types / 76 named) carries 0 render/component/template/markup/widget production, so a grammar patch could not be built from the language; R3 could express `uifigure(...)`/`uicontrol(...)` as ordinary `function_call` nodes (the construct IS a call), and R3 is NOT TAKEN because the edge it would publish has NO VALID TARGET: the contract is 'a component RENDERS another component', and a UI widget constructor's first argument is a PARENT CONTAINER object or a name/value list, not a declared component symbol — the runtime wires the tree, and the analyzer has no component model to point at. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (admitted files [0,3) of 3, transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): UI component constructor calls 0 (0 of the 23 widget constructor spellings appear; the constructor-name census is printed and empty); `.mlapp` files on the corpus tree 0 — and a `.mlapp` is a ZIP archive the ROUTER admits to no lane, so the App Designer route does not reach this lane's population either. FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): a UI constructor call whose first argument is an IDENTIFIER naming a DECLARED component symbol — counted 0 of 0 constructor sites; or a served-grammar production that carries a rendered-component reference — counted 0 of the 76 named node types. The `.mlapp` count turning non-zero on the corpus tree would also reopen the question, and the census prints it.

excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: RULED UNDECIDABLE (ONTOLOGICAL — MATLAB has no mixin/trait/composition clause; its only multi-parent construct is the SUPERCLASS LIST, and every base in it is an IS-A base whose members are INHERITED, which is `extends`, not a composed member set). THE LADDER WAS WALKED FIRST AND ITS RUNGS ARE UNAVAILABLE BY MEASUREMENT: R1/R2 — the served grammar's own inventory (grammars/tree-sitter-matlab/node-types.json, 148 node types / 76 named) carries `superclasses` (with `<` and `&`) as the inheritance production and 0 mixin/with/trait/include/composition production; a grammar patch would have to INVENT a construct MATLAB does not have. R3 exists — the `&` sites are ordinary `superclasses` children — and R3 is NOT TAKEN because the relation it would publish is a DIFFERENT relation from the one measured: a base named after `&` is still a superclass (the class IS-A it, and `isa()` answers true), so labelling it `mixes_in` would publish a conformance under the composition label. MEASURED SITES over the WHOLE admitted population (admitted files [0,3) of 3, transcript validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt): classes with a superclasses node 0, classes with TWO OR MORE bases (`&` sites) 0, superclass entries 0 — the construct is counted and is absent from this population. THE CORPUS-FREE HALF IS PINNED BY A FIXTURE: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/class-and-methods.m pins `classdef Report < BaseReport` as `extends` (a single base, which is inheritance, never relabelled). FALSIFIER (an instrument in the tree counts it): (1) a grammar production that composes a class from another class's member set WITHOUT an IS-A base (a `with`/`include`/`mixin` clause) — counted 0 of the 76 named node types; (2) a `classdef X < Y & Z` site where a base is NOT an IS-A superclass — counted 0 of 0 superclass entries over the population. A single such site refutes the ruling.

design_decision.description: MEASURED decisions forced by this lane's population, each naming the question, the answer and what pins it.

decisions.question: The population the gate admits for matlab is 3 `.m` files, all Objective-C by content (the router's `function ` substring matches English prose in comments). Should the lane measure them, exclude them, or report the router defect and stop?
decisions.answer: MEASURE THEM AND DISCLOSE. Production routes these files to the MATLAB grammar, so they ARE the lane's population; replacing or filtering them would be a workaround that makes the lane's denominator disagree with production's. Every count in this spec is over that population, `_population` states the content fact with the three trigger lines, and the fixture suite carries the doability evidence for the types the population cannot exercise. The routing defect itself is a report for the Lead (it is production code, not the analyzer).
decisions.pinnedBy: validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/census-constructs.ts + validation/m14/fixtures/matlab/measurements/matlab-constructs.txt (admitted 3, tracked 412 = 3 + 153 absent + 256 routed to objective-c), and the incoming gate's own line `corpus has 3 .m files across 2 repos`

decisions.question: Are `uses`, `contains`, `extends` IMPLEMENTED or GAPS when the admitted population emits 0 of each?
decisions.answer: IMPLEMENTED AND CORPUS-UNEXERCISED. The analyzer has an emission site for each and the fixtures fire all three, so they are not unimplemented; the population is silent because it contains no MATLAB declaration. The gate's stronger route requires a population claim AND a cited doability study for a zero, both supplied in `_implemented_measured`, and the corpusUnexercised list names each type so it can never be read as a double count.
decisions.pinnedBy: `bun script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang matlab` (5 pass, 0 fail) + the census's per-type emission counts

decisions.question: Is the lane's denominator the ten canonical types or the fourteen-value vocabulary?
decisions.answer: FOURTEEN. Three extended types are RULED (decorates, renders, mixes_in) with counts and falsifiers, so n = 11; the seven canonical types still to implement are GAPS inside n. That is the owner's bar and the coverage gate's default limb.
decisions.pinnedBy: this `coverage` block's arithmetic: implemented 4 + corpus-unexercised 0 (they are already in implemented) + gaps 7 = 11 = applicable

fleet_policy_that_applies_here: A PATH or URI target can never be a published name, so it is NEVER a resolution defect and is never counted as one — this applies directly to the 9 `import <Foundation/Foundation.h>`-shaped command sites the census found: they are Objective-C preprocessor headers, not MATLAB import targets.
A bare-identifier claim is verified through the TARGET itself (`verifyExternalClaim`), so `extFAIL` is expected to be 0.
The population is the gate's own sentence — `admitted files [a,b) of N` — and every claim here carries it.
